title: Luke Chapter 10 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 10 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 10 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Luke 10, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Lord appointed seventy others and sent them two by two
The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few
Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes
Heal the sick and say the kingdom of God is come nigh
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord appointed seventy others and sent them two by two
questions.explanation: Luke 10:1 states that the Lord appointed other seventy also and sent them two and two before his face.

questions.question: According to Luke 10, what did Jesus say about the harvest?
options: The harvest is small and the labourers are many
The harvest is great but the labourers are few
The harvest is ready and the labourers are ready
The harvest is not ready yet
questions.correctAnswer: The harvest is great but the labourers are few
questions.explanation: Luke 10:2 states, 'The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few.'

questions.question: In Luke 10, how did Jesus describe those He was sending out?
questions.correctAnswer: As lambs among wolves
questions.explanation: Luke 10:3 says, 'Behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.'

questions.question: What were the seventy instructed NOT to carry according to Luke 10?
questions.correctAnswer: Purse, scrip, or shoes
questions.explanation: Luke 10:4 commands the seventy to 'Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes.'

questions.question: What greeting were the seventy to give upon entering a house?
options: Welcome in the name of the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Peace be to this house
questions.explanation: Luke 10:5 states, 'first say, Peace be to this house.'

questions.question: According to Luke 10, what should happen if a 'son of peace' is in the house?
options: Your peace shall rest upon it
You must ask for food and shelter
questions.correctAnswer: Your peace shall rest upon it
questions.explanation: Luke 10:6 explains, 'if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it.'

questions.question: What instruction does Luke 10 give about moving from house to house?
options: Go from house to house to spread the message
Go not from house to house
Only enter houses of the wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: Go not from house to house
questions.explanation: Luke 10:7 states, 'Go not from house to house.'

questions.question: What were the seventy to do in a city if they were received, according to Luke 10?
options: Eat what is set before them
questions.correctAnswer: Eat what is set before them
questions.explanation: Luke 10:8 says, 'And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you.'

questions.question: What two things were the seventy instructed to do to the sick in the cities they entered?
options: Heal the sick and say the kingdom of God is come nigh
Feed the sick and pray for them
Anoint the sick with oil and baptize them
Give them money and take them to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Heal the sick and say the kingdom of God is come nigh
questions.explanation: Luke 10:9 states, 'And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.'

questions.question: If a city does not receive the seventy, what were they instructed to do according to Luke 10?
options: Stay and preach until they listen
Go into the streets of the city and shake off the dust of that city
Call the city leaders to repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Go into the streets of the city and shake off the dust of that city
questions.explanation: Luke 10:10-11 instructs them to 'go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say, Even the very dust of your city... we do wipe off against you.'

questions.question: According to Luke 10, which city will have a more tolerable judgment than the cities that reject the seventy?
questions.correctAnswer: Sodom
questions.explanation: Luke 10:12 states, 'it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.'

questions.question: True or False: Jesus sent out seventy others two by two before his face into every city and place.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 10:1 clearly states that the Lord appointed seventy others and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus told the seventy to pray that the Lord of the harvest would send forth labourers into his harvest.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 10:2 instructs to 'pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.'

questions.question: True or False: Luke 10 says the seventy were instructed to carry a purse and shoes during their mission.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 10:4 explicitly says, 'Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes.'

questions.question: True or False: Luke 10 commands the seventy to baptize those who receive them in the city.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: There is no mention in Luke 10:1-14 of baptizing; the instructions focus on greeting, healing, and preaching the kingdom of God.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 10 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 10 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about Capernaum?
options: It shall be thrust down to hell.
It will be exalted to heaven.
It will be a place of peace.
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be thrust down to hell.
questions.explanation: This is stated in Luke 10:15, where Jesus warns Capernaum of its impending judgment.

questions.question: What does Luke 10:16 promise will happen if someone despises Jesus' followers?
questions.correctAnswer: They despise Jesus.
questions.explanation: Luke 10:16 explains that to despise the followers of Jesus is to despise Jesus himself.

questions.question: What did the seventy disciples report back to Jesus?
options: The devils are subject unto us through thy name.
They did not understand their mission.
questions.correctAnswer: The devils are subject unto us through thy name.
questions.explanation: This is found in Luke 10:17, where the disciples express their joy in their authority over demons.

questions.question: What does Jesus say He witnessed regarding Satan?
options: Satan fell from heaven like lightning.
Satan will be defeated in the future.
Satan has no power over believers.
questions.correctAnswer: Satan fell from heaven like lightning.
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:18, Jesus describes a vision of Satan's fall, indicating his defeat.

questions.question: What power does Jesus give to His disciples in Luke 10:19?
options: Power to preach to the nations.
Power to heal the sick only.
Power to tread on serpents and scorpions.
questions.correctAnswer: Power to tread on serpents and scorpions.
questions.explanation: Luke 10:19 states that Jesus grants the disciples authority over dangerous creatures and the enemy.

questions.question: According to Luke 10:20, what should the disciples rejoice in?
options: That they can cast out demons.
That their names are written in heaven.
That they have power over sickness.
questions.correctAnswer: That their names are written in heaven.
questions.explanation: Jesus, in Luke 10:20, emphasizes that their ultimate joy should be in their salvation and relationship with God.

questions.question: What does Jesus thank the Father for in Luke 10:21?
options: For revealing truths to the wise.
For hiding things from the wise and prudent.
For giving wisdom to the disciples.
questions.correctAnswer: For hiding things from the wise and prudent.
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:21, Jesus expresses gratitude for God’s revelation to the humble while concealing it from the proud.

questions.question: What is said about who knows the Father and the Son in Luke 10:22?
options: Only the wise know the Father.
The Son reveals the Father to whom He chooses.
The Father is unknown to all.
questions.correctAnswer: The Son reveals the Father to whom He chooses.
questions.explanation: Luke 10:22 highlights the unique relationship between the Father and the Son, emphasizing their divine knowledge of each other.

questions.question: What blessing did Jesus declare about the eyes of His disciples in Luke 10:23?
options: They are blessed because they see miracles.
Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see.
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see.
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:23, Jesus affirms the privilege of His disciples to witness His ministry and teachings.

questions.question: What did many prophets and kings desire to see, according to Luke 10:24?
options: The things which ye see, and have not seen them.
questions.correctAnswer: The things which ye see, and have not seen them.
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:24, Jesus notes that many great figures longed to witness His works and teachings, which the disciples were experiencing.

questions.question: What must one do to inherit eternal life, according to the lawyer's question in Luke 10:25?
options: Follow the commandments and love your neighbor.
questions.correctAnswer: Follow the commandments and love your neighbor.
questions.explanation: Luke 10:25 reveals the essence of the law as loving God and one's neighbor, which is essential for eternal life.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen if the lawyer obeyed the law in Luke 10:28?
questions.correctAnswer: He shall live.
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:28, Jesus affirms that obedience to the commandment leads to eternal life.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus rejoiced in spirit about the revelation to the humble?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is true as found in Luke 10:21, where Jesus expresses joy and gratitude for God's revelation to the humble.

questions.question: Is it false that Jesus sent the disciples without any provisions?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This is false as Jesus instructed them not to carry provisions in Luke 10:4.

questions.question: Is it false that many kings desired to hear the teachings of Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This is false; many prophets and kings desired to see and hear what the disciples experienced, as stated in Luke 10:24.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 10 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 10.

questions.question: In Jesus' parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-35), which individual first passed by the man who was robbed and left half dead?
questions.correctAnswer: A certain priest
questions.explanation: Luke 10:31 states that a certain priest came down that way and passed by on the other side, not helping the injured man.

questions.question: What did the Samaritan do after binding the wounded man's wounds in Luke 10:34?
options: He left him at the roadside
He poured in oil and wine, set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn
He gave him money and told him to go to a healer
questions.correctAnswer: He poured in oil and wine, set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn
questions.explanation: Luke 10:34 records the Samaritan binding the man's wounds with oil and wine, placing him on his own beast, and bringing him to an inn to care for him.

questions.question: How much money did the Samaritan give to the innkeeper for the care of the wounded man in Luke 10:35?
questions.correctAnswer: Two pence
questions.explanation: Luke 10:35 states the Samaritan gave two pence to the host to take care of the man and promised to repay any extra expenses.

questions.question: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who ultimately is identified as the neighbor to the man who fell among thieves?
questions.correctAnswer: The Samaritan
questions.explanation: Luke 10:36-37 show Jesus asking which of the three was neighbor, and the answer given is the one who showed mercy—the Samaritan.

questions.question: What complaint did Martha make to Jesus when Mary was sitting at His feet in Luke 10:40?
options: Lord, dost Thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone?
Why do You not heal my brother?
Why do You speak in parables?
Why does Mary not help in the kitchen?
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, dost Thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone?
questions.explanation: Luke 10:40 records Martha's complaint that Mary left her to serve alone and asked Jesus to tell her to help.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Luke 10:42, what did Mary choose that 'shall not be taken away from her'?
questions.correctAnswer: That good part
questions.explanation: Luke 10:42 shows Jesus affirming that Mary chose the good part—listening to His word—which shall not be taken away.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'σπλαγχνίζομαι' (splanchnizomai) used in Luke 10:33 mean?
options: To have compassion or deep pity
questions.correctAnswer: To have compassion or deep pity
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:33, the Samaritan 'had compassion' on the man; the Greek word 'σπλαγχνίζομαι' means to feel deep inward compassion, often translated as mercy or pity.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:30-37)?
questions.correctAnswer: Parable
questions.explanation: Luke 10:30-37 presents a parable, a narrative device Jesus used to teach moral or spiritual lessons through storytelling.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the command to love one's neighbor as seen in Luke 10:27?
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 19:18
questions.explanation: Luke 10:27 quotes loving your neighbor as yourself, a command originally found in Leviticus 19:18.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of mercy shown in the Good Samaritan parable (Luke 10:30-37)?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 25:35-40
questions.explanation: Matthew 25:35-40 echoes the theme of compassion and mercy toward others as serving Christ Himself, similar to the Good Samaritan's mercy in Luke 10.

questions.question: What instruction did Jesus give to His seventy disciples regarding their manners when entering a house in Luke 10:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Say, 'Peace be to this house'
questions.explanation: Luke 10:5 directs the disciples to greet each house with 'Peace be to this house' as a blessing and sign of goodwill.

questions.question: Which historical-cultural context explains why the priest and Levite might have avoided helping the injured man in Luke 10:31-32?
options: Concern about ritual purity laws and touching a potentially dead body
They did not see the man
questions.correctAnswer: Concern about ritual purity laws and touching a potentially dead body
questions.explanation: Jewish priests and Levites observed strict purity laws (Leviticus 21), which could make them ceremonially unclean if they touched a dead or dying man, possibly influencing their avoidance in Luke 10:31-32.

questions.question: How does the story of Mary and Martha in Luke 10:38-42 illustrate the theme of discipleship in the New Testament?
options: Prioritizing spiritual listening over busy service
questions.correctAnswer: Prioritizing spiritual listening over busy service
questions.explanation: Luke 10:39-42 contrasts Martha's distracted serving with Mary's attentive listening at Jesus' feet, emphasizing the New Testament theme that discipleship involves hearing and obeying Jesus above all else.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 10:20 encourages rejoicing because the disciples' names are written in heaven rather than because of their ability to cast out spirits.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 10:20 explicitly instructs rejoicing not in spirits being subject, but because names are written in heaven.

questions.question: True or False: In Luke 10:4, Jesus commands the seventy disciples to carry purses, scrips, and shoes as they go.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 10:4 instructs the disciples to carry neither purse, scrip, nor shoes, emphasizing reliance on God's provision.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 10 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 10 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 10:2 teach about God's provision for salvation?
options: God provides laborers for the harvest through prayer
Salvation is earned by human labor
The harvest is small and limited
Laborers are sufficient without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God provides laborers for the harvest through prayer
questions.explanation: Luke 10:2 emphasizes that because the harvest is great but laborers are few, believers must pray to the Lord of the harvest to send laborers, indicating God's sovereign provision in salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's authority is taught in Luke 10:19?
options: Christ grants believers authority over all the power of the enemy
Believers have no power over evil forces
Authority over evil is only given to angels
Power over evil is gained through personal merit
questions.correctAnswer: Christ grants believers authority over all the power of the enemy
questions.explanation: Luke 10:19 shows that Jesus gives His followers authority to overcome dangerous spiritual forces, demonstrating His sovereign power over evil.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning revelation to the humble is taught in Luke 10:21?
options: God reveals truths to the humble rather than the wise and prudent
Wisdom and prudence guarantee divine revelation
Revelation is only for the learned
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals truths to the humble rather than the wise and prudent
questions.explanation: Luke 10:21 states that God has hidden certain things from the wise and prudent but revealed them to babes, teaching that divine revelation comes through humility.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 10:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Omnipotence
questions.explanation: In Luke 10:18, Jesus declares He saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven, demonstrating God's omnipotence over Satan's defeat.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 10:21 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Luke 10:21 shows God's sovereign will in revealing truths to the humble according to His good pleasure, highlighting divine sovereignty.

questions.question: How does Luke 10:1–12 prepare for the Great Commission theme found in Matthew 28?
options: By sending disciples to proclaim the kingdom and heal, it prefigures worldwide mission
It focuses only on local Jewish ministry with no global outlook
It establishes a priestly caste for temple rituals
It rejects the idea of mission work
questions.correctAnswer: By sending disciples to proclaim the kingdom and heal, it prefigures worldwide mission
questions.explanation: Luke 10:1–12 shows Jesus commissioning seventy to preach and heal, anticipating the later universal mission charge in Matthew 28.

questions.question: How does the parable in Luke 10:30-37 connect redemptive history with Old Testament law?
options: It fulfills the command to love one's neighbor by redefining neighborliness beyond ethnic boundaries
It denies any obligation to the law
It restricts neighbor love only to fellow Jews
It teaches salvation by works alone
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the command to love one's neighbor by redefining neighborliness beyond ethnic boundaries
questions.explanation: The parable in Luke 10:30-37 expands the law's neighborly love command by showing mercy to a Samaritan, an outsider, thus applying the law inclusively.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Luke 10:16 and Luke 10:22 teach about Christ's identity and mission?
options: Christ's authority is divine and He reveals the Father to those chosen by Him
Christ is only a prophet with no divine authority
Christ's mission is independent of the Father
Christ is unknown even to His disciples
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's authority is divine and He reveals the Father to those chosen by Him
questions.explanation: Luke 10:16 shows the authority of Christ's messengers as His own, and 10:22 reveals that only the Son reveals the Father, affirming Christ's divine identity and mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 10:27 and Luke 10:37 teach about the nature of the law and mercy?
options: True fulfillment of the law involves loving God and neighbor, which is expressed through merciful action
The law is abolished and replaced by mercy
Mercy is unrelated to the law
Only ritual observance fulfills the law
questions.correctAnswer: True fulfillment of the law involves loving God and neighbor, which is expressed through merciful action
questions.explanation: Luke 10:27 states the law's command to love God and neighbor; 10:37 illustrates this love as mercy in action, merging law and grace.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 10:20 and Luke 10:21 teach about joy and divine revelation?
options: Joy in salvation is rooted not in power over spirits but in assurance of being known by God
Joy depends on earthly success and power
Revelation is given to the proud
questions.correctAnswer: Joy in salvation is rooted not in power over spirits but in assurance of being known by God
questions.explanation: Luke 10:20 urges rejoicing in names written in heaven rather than spiritual authority, and 10:21 shows joy in God's revealing to the humble, linking joy to revelation and salvation.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Luke 10:8-12 teaches that rejection of the gospel is unimportant. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Rejection has serious consequences and warns of judgment
Rejection is encouraged as normal and without consequences
The gospel is optional and has no urgency
Jesus ignores rejection and does not respond to it
questions.correctAnswer: Rejection has serious consequences and warns of judgment
questions.explanation: Luke 10:10-12 teaches that cities rejecting the message face judgment more severe than Sodom, indicating rejection is grave.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 10:42 teach about priorities in discipleship?
options: Choosing to focus on Christ's teaching is the 'one thing needful' that cannot be taken away
Service and works are the only important aspects
Busyness in ministry is the highest calling
questions.correctAnswer: Choosing to focus on Christ's teaching is the 'one thing needful' that cannot be taken away
questions.explanation: Luke 10:42 contrasts Martha's distraction with Mary's choice to sit and hear Jesus, highlighting the primacy of devotion over activity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 10:22 particularly demonstrate in Christ's relationship with the Father?
options: Mutual knowledge and revelation between Father and Son
questions.correctAnswer: Mutual knowledge and revelation between Father and Son
questions.explanation: Luke 10:22 states no one knows the Son except the Father, and vice versa, highlighting the unique divine relationship and revelation.

questions.question: How does the healing and proclamation in Luke 10:9 illustrate the kingdom of God?
options: The kingdom of God is both proclaimed and manifest through healing
The kingdom is only a future hope with no present reality
Healing is unrelated to the kingdom message
The kingdom is a political kingdom only
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of God is both proclaimed and manifest through healing
questions.explanation: Luke 10:9 links the healing of the sick with the proclamation that the kingdom of God is near, showing the kingdom's present and active power.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 10:4 and Luke 10:7 teach about reliance on God in mission?
options: Missionaries are called to depend on God's provision and hospitality rather than their own resources
Missionaries should prepare extensively with supplies
Self-sufficiency is the basis for mission success
Missionaries are to isolate themselves from local communities
questions.correctAnswer: Missionaries are called to depend on God's provision and hospitality rather than their own resources
questions.explanation: Luke 10:4 commands going without purse or scrip, and 10:7 instructs staying with one host, emphasizing dependence on God and community.
